analysis:
MARKET REGIME — DOWNTREND ACTIVE: SPY is -5.2% below its 50-day SMA with a negative 20d slope (-1.06%). This is the single most important input today. Quality-value strategies suffer their worst drawdowns during broad market selloffs, not from name-specific blowups. Deploying new capital aggressively into a confirmed downtrend is the surest way to destroy the account's compounding baseline.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW — Five positions consuming 84% of equity with only $10,051 of headroom remaining for new buys. That alone argues for a quiet hand.

(1) AMP (-9.01%, $9,458): This is the most urgent flag. Ameriprise is down 9% from average cost in a deteriorating macro environment for financials/wealth management. Broad market weakness compounds the drawdown risk here. If the original stop was placed around 12-15% below entry (~$464-$478), it has not been technically triggered yet, but the position is in drawdown territory that warrants active monitoring. The thesis relied on a basing setup continuing — with SPY in confirmed downtrend and AMP approaching its lower bound, holders should ask whether the original trend premise still holds. No action today because the stop has not been hit, but this is a 'one more leg down and exit' situation.

(2) ULTA (+4.31%): Largest position ($28,845 / ~30% of equity — right at the 25% hard cap on market value). Already a winner; let it run but be alert to any thesis break.

(3) UHS (+3.40%): Also in the screened candidate list showing uptrend with basing. Performing well relative to market. No action needed.

(4) FOXA (-0.60%): Essentially flat. No action needed.

(5) ADSK (+0.71%): Barely positive. No action needed.

NEW BUYS — Zero new trades proposed. Three compounding reasons: (a) market regime is DOWNTREND — the base rate for new longs initiated in confirmed downtrends is unfavorable; (b) only $10,051 of deployment headroom remains, too thin to size any position with proper risk management (1.5% portfolio heat formula yields $1,435 risk budget; at ~5% typical stop that implies a $28,700 position, almost 3x available cash); (c) the portfolio's Sortino ratio of -11.77 and 1.05 profit factor tell us edge is marginal at best — this is exactly the environment where sitting on cash is the alpha. No candidate clears the hurdle of genuinely asymmetric setup + adequate sizing capacity + favorable macro backdrop simultaneously. Cash is the position.
